title: lena-thompson-people-ops-self-notes-manager-prep-2026-q1
content:
Manager prep + self-notes (Q1 2026)

Purpose:
- Capture wins, blockers, and asks before 1:1 with Maya (people ops manager) on 2026-03-03.
- Draft talking points for calibration / compensation conversation and promotion readiness.

High-level wins (since last cycle):
- Launched manager onboarding playbook v1 (pilot): reduced new manager ramp time (survey) from ~45d to ~28d for the pilot cohort. Key metrics: 12 managers onboarded, avg NPS 4.1/5, two managers reported higher confidence in 1:1s.
- Rolled out quarterly pulse survey and automated reporting in Looker: 420 responses (85% response rate target hit for pilot team), identified top themes: workload, clarity on career ladders.
- Cross-functional ops: partnered with Eng Ops to document headcount forecasting flow — created a shared sheet and set weekly sync; removed duplicate requests, estimated 10h/week saved across hiring managers.

Areas I owned (specific impact):
- Manager onboarding project (project lead): design, content, vendor coordination for micro-learning modules. Next steps: scale to AMER/EU launches, add translations.
- Career ladder refresh (contributor): drafted new IC progression language for IC3 -> IC4; ran 3 feedback sessions. Outcome: clearer rubric for scope-of-impact examples.
- Hiring process cleanup: implemented panel interviewer training, decreased interview loop time by ~1.3 days on average for product roles.

Challenges / blockers:
- Bandwidth: multiple overlapping pilots (manager onboarding, pulse survey, ladder refresh) — need a clear priority slate for Q2 to avoid burnout.
- Measurement gaps: still missing baseline for manager effectiveness beyond self-report; want to integrate manager-level performance signals (team retention, deliverable velocity) but need Eng support.
- Headcount volatility: recruiting delays pushing off key hires for the ops analytics role; this impacts our ability to scale the dashboards.

Asks for manager (Maya):
- Headcount prioritization: request approval to move one contractor budget to a full-time req (ops-analyst) to support dashboards and data quality. Rationale: immediate ROI in reporting cadence and freeing up 6-8 hours/week of my time for strategy.
- Calibration support: ask for advocacy in the upcoming compensation calibration cycle — propose leveling case for promotion to Senior People Ops (timeline below).
- Time: blocked for 2 weeks in late March for vendor kickoff — ask for bandwidth reprioritization or temporary reallocation of meeting ownership.

Promotion readiness notes (case for Senior People Ops):
- Scope growth: moved from program-level execution to leading cross-functional product (manager onboarding) and policy work (career ladder).
- Impact: measurable time savings (headcount process), improved manager NPS, pilot adoption signals.
- Leadership: mentored two junior ops colleagues, led stakeholder syncs with Eng, Product, and Recruiting.
- Risks/gaps: need clearer metrics tying manager onboarding to business outcomes (eng retention, IC promotion velocity). Proposed mitigation: hire ops-analyst and run a 6-month evaluation with concrete KPIs.

Suggested compensation/promotion timeline:
- Submit leveling packet in April 2026 cycle.
- Request market comp banding +10-12% if leveled to Senior.
- Proposed promotion effective start: 2026-06-01 (aligns with FY26 mid-year review).

1:1 talking points (ordered):
1) Quick wins recap (1-2 mins).
2) Current stretch workload and bandwidth concerns — propose concrete tradeoffs (which projects to deprioritize).
3) Headcount ask: convert contractor -> FTE (ops-analyst).
4) Promotion readiness: review evidence and next steps for leveling packet.
5) Support needed: calibration advocacy + temporary reassignments for vendor kickoff.
6) Career development: mentor plan and potential stretch projects (lead cross-functional onboarding for EU).

Data / backup to bring:
- Manager onboarding pilot deck (pilot metrics slide).
- Pulse survey summary export (CSV) + Looker link.
- Headcount forecasting sheet with proposed contractor reallocation.
- Example ladder language snippets and feedback notes.

Notes to self (framing language):
- "I enjoy building repeatable systems that scale manager capability — want to move from 'doer' to 'designer' of programs."
- Keep the ask simple: one headcount + promotion timeframe. Show ROI and risk mitigation.
- Emphasize mentorship and cross-functional leadership; have concrete examples ready.

Open questions I want Maya's input on:
- Is the company more likely to approve an FTE conversion this quarter or next, given hiring freeze risk?
- How should I present ladder changes during calibration to avoid triggering forced-regrades?
- Are there internal stakeholders I should loop in early for the Senior case (HRBP, Recruiting lead)?

Next actions (before 1:1):
- Export pilot metrics + short one-pager (by 2026-03-02).
- Draft promotion leveling packet outline (by 2026-03-10).
- Prepare compensation benchmark notes (levels + market data).
- Send pre-read to Maya with 24-48h ahead of 1:1.

Longer-term goals (6-12 months):
- Build a manager effectiveness dashboard (engagement, retention, promotion velocity).
- Scale manager onboarding to global cohorts (AMER/EU) with localized content.
- Own career ladder lifecycle: maintenance cadence, feedback loops, and promotion readiness workshops.

Random scratch ideas / brainstorm (keep short):
- Micro-mentorship pairing program for new managers (15 min/week).
- Office hours for interview calibration — tie to hiring metrics.
- Quarterly manager "roundtables" to surface sticky policy issues.

Versioning / history:
- v0.1 (2026-02-25) initial draft notes.
- v0.2 (2026-03-01) added metric references and asks for manager.

"Notes to future me": keep this doc updated after the 1:1; capture Maya's feedback verbatim and action items with owners and dates.
